subject: Re: Orion AI — Dedicated burst tempo, SLA carveouts and autoscale walkthrough
messages:
From: Ellis Zhao <ellis@orionai.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated burst needs — quick intro and plan

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We loved the latency numbers but want to lock down how Redwood would handle the weekly training-induced inference spikes we see (approx. 6-10x bursts for 2–3 hours). Key asks from my side:

- Can we get a clear SLA carveout during scheduled retraining windows?
- How does autoscale behave when queueing hits the shoulder: eviction, throttling, headroom guarantees?
- Will we be able to reserve a shoulder slab and still allow short-lived ephemeral bursts across regions?

I can loop in procurement if we get a baseline design. Attaching our peak profile (summary).

Appreciate a short walk-through early this week.

Best,
Ellis
Head of Infrastructure, Orion AI

Attachment: orion-burst-draft-v1.pdf (summary CSVs + perf traces)

From: aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Zhao <ellis@orionai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated burst needs — quick intro and plan

Ellis — great to hear. Short answer: yes, we can support the weekly 6–10x spikes with a combination of shoulder reservations + transient burst slabs, and deterministic SLOs for your tier.

Proposed next steps:
1) Karthik and I run your attached profile through our capacity simulator to map to concrete GPU-slab sizes.
2) We draft two concrete burst policies: 
   - "Shielded Shoulder" (reserved shoulder + limited eviction window)
   - "Opportunistic Ephemeral" (best-effort preemptible slab for short tails)
3) Ben to provide pricing delta for the two approaches + a provisional addendum we can include in the Dedicated contract.

Can you confirm the weekly retrain window (day/time) and whether cross-region bursting is allowed? Also, can procurement/finance be cc'd on the follow-ups?

Thanks,
Aisha
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Zhao <ellis@orionai.com>, aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated burst needs — quick intro and plan

Ellis — quick technical readout from my side (digestible bullets):

- With your profile, the clean mapping is: 1x reserved + 1.5x shoulder slab + ephemeral pool sized to ~25% of your burst ceiling. That gives deterministic latency for 85% of tokens and bounded fallback for the tail.
- Autoscale behavior: we run a two-tier scale controller. Fast path (seconds): spin ephemeral workers; Slow path (minutes): grow shoulder slab if sustained for >30min.
- Eviction policy: LRU-based eviction of preemptible workers; protected workloads pinned to shoulder slab will not be evicted during the declared retrain window.
- QoS guardrails: token-weighted admission control — short requests get priority. We can configure per-route weights for your critical inference endpoints.

I'll attach a quick spreadsheet mapping your peak qps to GPU slab counts; Ben/Laura can use this for pricing and contractual language.

-Karthik
Lead Capacity Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-burst-tiers.xlsx

From: Ellis Zhao <ellis@orionai.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Nina Park <nina@orionai.com>, procurement@orionai.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 10:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated burst needs — quick intro and plan

Thanks both — this looks good. A couple clarifications before we run the simulator:

- Our retrain window is Wed 02:00–05:00 PT (weekly). During those three hours, we expect sustained 8x baseline QPS and occasional peaks up to 12x for short (5–10 min) durations.
- Cross-region bursts are allowed but must be limited: primary region + one DR region. Cost allocation must attribute ephemeral usage to the primary subscription.

Procurement is on cc — they will want wording for: guaranteed shoulder capacity during retrain windows, exceptions for force majeure, and a clean billing line for ephemeral bursts (meta: hourly slab increments).

Could you provide a short example SLA clause and a sample autoscale timeline we can drop into our SOW?

-Ellis

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Zhao <ellis@orionai.com>, procurement@orionai.com
Cc: aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated burst needs — quick intro and plan

Ellis / Procurement — putting pricing and contract-level language into one place. Summary:

- Option A (Shielded Shoulder): Monthly fee for reserved shoulder slab + metered ephemeral at $/GPU-hour. Shoulder reserved for your weekly retrain window; eviction protections included.
- Option B (Opportunistic Ephemeral): Smaller reserved shoulder, higher reliance on ephemeral pool; lower monthly commit, higher burst rates.

Sample SLA snippet (draft):
"Redwood will maintain reserved shoulder capacity described in Schedule A during Customer-declared maintenance windows. During declared windows, Redwood will not evict applications pinned to the reserved shoulder slab except for force majeure. Latency SLOs apply to requests served from reserved shoulder; requests served from ephemeral pools are best-effort with prioritized admission to reduce tail latency."

Autoscale timeline (example):
- 0–30s: admission controller prioritizes short requests, spins ephemeral fast-path workers
- 30s–15m: scale ephemeral pool up to pre-defined cap
- >15m sustained: orchestrator expands shoulder slab (billing triggers at 1-hour granularity)

I also opened the HubSpot deal and attached the provisional addendum. DocuSign will be available once you pick Option A vs B.

DocuSign (placeholder): https://docusign.com/redwood/orion/ORION-DEAL-2026-11
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20m call to finalize wording.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Nina Park <nina@orionai.com>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, procurement@orionai.com
Cc: aisha_rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, ellis@orionai.com
Date: Sun, 05 Dec 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated burst needs — quick intro and plan

Ben / Aisha — procurement here. We reviewed the sample SLA and timeline; a couple of small asks before legal signs: 

1) Add a clause that ephemeral billing is capped at X% of monthly commit for the first 6 months (we'll propose 20% to limit cost exposure).
2) Require a 24-hour advance notice for shoulder slab expansion outside declared windows (to help our internal capacity planning).
3) Please confirm the regional attribution mechanics for ephemeral usage on the invoice.

If you can incorporate those three items into the addendum, we can route to legal and push the DocuSign. Happy to have a quick call Tue morning PT.

Regards,
Nina Park
Procurement, Orion AI
